title: Tufts University Biomedical Engineering Research Scholars (TUBERS)
text: The Tufts University Biomedical Engineering Research Scholars (TUBERS) Program offers high school students with an interest in biomedical engineering research the opportunity to gain practical experience over a six-week summer period. Participants will engage in hands-on work within Tufts' biomedical engineering labs, where they will learn experimental protocols, test hypotheses, and contribute to specific projects. They will receive academic guidance from undergraduate and graduate students involved in the program, as well as their research mentors. The program is free of charge and encourages applications from underrepresented backgrounds. While participants are responsible for their own transportation to campus, housing is not provided for out-of-area students. The program's objectives include exposing students to a wide range of biomedical engineering techniques, providing in-depth study of a specific scientific field, guiding them through the scientific method in their projects, facilitating the presentation of their findings, showcasing the work of professional researchers, and fostering critical and independent thinking. Students are encouraged to utilize their projects for participation in science competitions, offering the potential for honors and scholarship awards.
requirements: To be considered for the Tufts University Biomedical Engineering Research Scholars (TUBERS) Program, applicants must be 16 years old by the start of the program on July 5th, 2023 and show a strong interest in biomedical research. Participants must be committed to working for approximately 6 weeks during the summer in the Biomedical Engineering labs at Tufts, learning about research techniques and a particular field of study in depth while carrying out all steps of the scientific method in their project. Individuals from underrepresented backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. Participants are expected to find their own transportation to the Tufts University Medford campus and there is no housing provided for out-of-area students. Students are encouraged to use their projects to participate in local and national science competitions. The program is free and successful applicants will learn a broad array of biomedical engineering research techniques, gain academic guidance from undergraduates and graduate students involved with the program and their research mentors, observe the work of professional researchers, present their findings to others in the program, parents, and teachers, learn to think critically and independently, and gain a deeper understanding of a particular field of science.

title: Senate Page Program
text: The North Carolina Senate Page Program offers high school students in grades 10-12 an immersive experience in the state's legislative process. Selected pages witness firsthand the lawmaking process and assist senators and staff during legislative sessions on the Senate Chamber floor. Their responsibilities include attending daily sessions and committee meetings, delivering messages and materials, answering phones, distributing documents, and running errands. To participate, students must be sponsored by a North Carolina senator, maintain good academic standing, and submit an application to their sponsor. The program spans several weeks throughout the year, with pages receiving a weekly stipend of $150 for expenses.
address: North Carolina Senate, Legislative Building, Room 1029, Raleigh, NC 27601-2808
requirements: To be considered for the North Carolina Senate Page Program, applicants must be in grades ten, eleven, or twelve and sponsored by a member of the North Carolina Senate. Applicants must also be in good academic standing at their school and have prior approval from their principal if serving as a page during the school year. The selection process is highly competitive, with senators recommending individuals to be appointed by the President Pro Tempore of the Senate on a first-come, first-served basis. Pages must be able to attend sessions from Monday afternoon to Thursday afternoon of their assigned week, work in appropriate business attire, and receive a stipend of $150 or thirty hours of community service. Pages are expected to participate in daily senate sessions, committee meetings, and provide office assistance. Lodging is not provided, and pages must cover their lunch and personal expenses. Only a limited number of parking spaces are available for self-commuting pages. Finally, Senate Pages are encouraged to be helpful, cordial, and polite, and to avoid wearing jeans, tennis shoes, or thong sandals (flip flops) while on duty.

text: The Berkeley Lab Director's Apprenticeship Program (BLDAP) is a STEM program for high school students in 10th and 11th grades in the Bay area, particularly Alameda, San Francisco, and West Contra Costa counties. title: High School Internship Program in Integrated Mathematical Oncology
text: The High School Student Internship Program in Integrated Mathematical Oncology (HIP IMO) is an immersive 8-week summer program at the Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida. Designed for high school students aged 16 or older, HIP IMO offers interdisciplinary team science research experiences tailored to individual interests and abilities. Under the guidance of faculty and scientists in the Integrated Mathematical Oncology department, students engage in research projects, gaining access to necessary computer equipment and software. Selected participants receive a $1,000 scholarship and are expected to attend daily from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Throughout the program, students develop oral presentation skills by delivering a 15-minute presentation at the HIP IMO research day and submit a three-page scientific report at its conclusion.
requirements: To be considered for the HIP IMO (High School Student Internship Program in Integrated Mathematical Oncology) program, applicants should be high school students aged 16 years or older by the time of the internship, interested in interdisciplinary cancer research careers, and have a keen interest in developing lifelong research skills. The program is designed for motivated students, and applicants should be able to commit to attending the program daily for eight weeks during traditional Hillsborough County public school summer break. Interested students should fill out an application form, which can be accessed either in Microsoft Word or PDF formats, on or before February 1, 2023. The completed applications should be emailed to hipimo@moffitt.org, and teachers should email letters of support by the same deadline to the same email. Notification of acceptance will be sent to applicants by end-February or early March 2023. All HIP IMO interns are subject to a drug screening, background check, and tuberculosis test (TB) before arrival at Moffitt as part of safety and security concerns. The program does not provide a stipend and is not capable of funding intern housing. Selected students will receive a $1,000 scholarship during the first week of HIP IMO.

title: The Introductory College Level Experience in Microbiology
text: The iCLEM program is a paid summer science intensive designed for economically disadvantaged high school sophomores and juniors. The program aims to expand students' knowledge of biotechnology, microbiology, and biofuels, as well as introduce them to career exploration and preparation for the college application process. Students will complete a research project in a modern laboratory setting mentored by JBEI researchers and UC undergrads. The program will be hybrid in format, with in-person instruction at the Emeryville, CA laboratory 2-3 days a week and remote instruction on other days. Participants will receive a stipend of $3,000, and they will also have opportunities to learn about college admission requirements and financial aid, and to explore careers through discussions with STEM professionals and visits to local biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies. To apply, students must meet eligibility requirements and submit a transcript, personal statement, "Why are you applying for iCLEM" statement, and a teacher's letter of reference.
requirements: To be considered for the iCLEM internship program, applicants must meet the following requirements: (1) be at least 15 years old by December 31, 2022, (2) be a currently enrolled sophomore or junior at a high school located in Alameda, Contra Costa, or San Francisco County, (3) be a US citizen, permanent resident, or DACA recipient, (4) have a GPA of at least 2.5 and have passed Algebra 1 and Biology, (5) have an annual household income of less than $104,445 in Alameda County, $100,780 in Contra Costa County, or $122,565 in San Francisco County, with possible additions to the income limitations for larger families, and (6) be able to commit to attending the program from June 20, 2023, to July 28, 2023. In addition, applicants must submit a current transcript, a personal statement describing their life goals and background, a statement detailing why they are a good fit for the iCLEM program, and the name and email address of a teacher willing to provide a letter of reference upon request. The application process is highly competitive and rigorous, with emphasis placed on a student's background, teacher recommendations, and desire to do science and work hard during the summer.

title: Research in Science & Engineering (RISE) Internship/Practicum
text: The RISE program, offered by Boston University Summer Term, is a six-week internship/practicum designed for domestic high school juniors with a passion for STEM subjects. The program offers two tracks: Internship and Practicum. In the Internship track, students engage in research projects under the guidance of postdoctoral fellows, graduate students, and distinguished faculty, working 40 hours weekly. The Practicum track provides a structured syllabus on computational neurobiology within a research environment led by a BU instructor, featuring four hours of group research in the afternoon and two-hour lectures in the morning. Both tracks include workshops focused on developing academic and professional skills, poster symposium presentations, and weekly interactions with biotech or pharmaceutical firms. Through the program, students gain proficiency in reading research papers, networking in the engineering and science fields, and understanding research ethics and the scientific process. With over 40 years of experience, the RISE program has played a significant role in launching the careers of many students in science, engineering, and research.

The Internship track allows students to work on research projects supervised by faculty members, postdoctoral fellows, and graduate students, focusing on developing technical and analytical skills, insight into the scientific process, and STEM knowledge while spending 40 hours per week on their projects. On the other hand, the Practicum track, focused on computational neurobiology, is ideal for students who prefer a more structured research environment. Students in this track will be tasked with group research in a university laboratory setting guided by a BU instructor. Both tracks include weekly workshops aimed at building academic and professional skills, as well as off-site or on-site interactions with local biotech or pharmaceutical companies. A laptop capable of running programming software is required for Practicum students. Each student will present their research findings at the Poster Symposium that concludes the program.

title: Next Generation STEM Internship Program
text: The Next Generation STEM Internship Program (NGSI) offers rising juniors and seniors from select counties the opportunity to engage in STEM projects with researchers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). Participants gain invaluable experience working alongside renowned scientists and engineers, while also benefiting from professional development activities such as workshops, lab tours, lectures, poster sessions, seminars, and networking events. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents, have a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0, be at least 16 years of age, and be rising juniors/seniors or recent graduates. The program provides weekly stipends of up to $500 for 40 hours of participation each week.

title: Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program (RSYEP)
text: The Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program offers teenagers aged 15 to 18 within Raleigh city limits an opportunity to gain workforce skills and experience through a six-week summer work program. Participants work for the City of Raleigh from late June to early August, attending mandatory training and orientation sessions prior to the start of the program. In addition to work experience, participants engage in skill-building and training sessions, and benefit from networking opportunities. To participate, individuals must be available for the program's duration, attend orientation and training sessions, and provide an NC State Issued ID or other documentation showing residency. The program prioritizes the health and safety of participants and staff, requiring full Covid-19 vaccination for in-person or hybrid work, while offering a virtual work option for those who prefer remote work.
requirements: Applicants to the Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program must be between the ages of 15 and 18 as of May 31, 2023, live within the Raleigh city limits, and be available to work from June 20 to August 4. They must attend the mandatory in-person program orientation on May 20 and not miss more than four program days or be enrolled in summer school. They must be the only one in their household participating in the program and have computer and internet access if they choose the virtual option. Additionally, applicants must have an NC State Issued ID, Learner’s Permit, Driver’s License, or current school report card that shows a Raleigh zip code at the time of interview, with no exceptions. Finally, all new employees must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 for in-person or hybrid work, and for virtual/remote employment, vaccination is not required.

title: UnitedHealth Group's Unified High School Internship Experience
text: The Optum High School Internship Program, offered by UnitedHealth Group, provides rising juniors and seniors with an immersive experience in the healthcare industry. This paid internship, lasting 6-8 weeks, offers remote opportunities in certain locations. Interns engage in real-world healthcare challenges, working alongside experts in IT, finance, human resources, product management, and more. The program emphasizes empathy, social impact, diversity, and inclusion, fostering the development of future healthcare leaders. Through hands-on experience, interns gain exposure to various career paths within Optum, a leading health services and innovation company dedicated to enhancing healthcare delivery, quality, and efficiency.
requirements: The requirements for applicants to be considered for the UnitedHealth Group's Unified High School Internship Experience are as follows: they must currently be enrolled in high school as a rising junior or senior, must be authorized to work in the US, and must meet all requirements listed on the UnitedHealth Group application form, including submitting their resume. Additionally, applicants must live within a commutable distance to one of the specified locations or be located in Raleigh, NC; Basking Ridge, NJ, Cypress, CA, Eden Prairie, MN, District of Columbia, Texas and Georgia, which will allow for remote work. Authorization to work in the US is necessary and F-1 visa holders with Curricular Practical Training (CPT) or Optional Practical Training (OPT), TN visa holders, current H-1B visa holders, and/or those requiring green card sponsorship will not be considered. Applicants exhibiting a willingness to learn by asking questions and contributing ideas, demonstrating attention to detail, time-management skills, effective communication and written skills, and the ability to collaborate with others as part of a team are preferred.
